plan.title: Crohn's ileum: hallmark GSVA scores, inflamed vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question asks for a per-sample score for every MSigDB Hallmark signature and which signatures differ between Crohn's-inflamed and control ileum (6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples). The design has one flagged quality issue: sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median, so QC must inspect it (not silently drop it) per rule R-0008/R-0030. The plan follows the grounded procedure: (1) sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, explicit library-size/detected-gene reporting for sample_01) to decide, with a stated reason, whether it stays; (2) DESeq2 filtering/normalization/Wald test with apeglm shrinkage to get a gene-level differential expression backbone, run on the counts as delivered since the profile does not establish that Salmon's length correction was applied — this is stated as a caveat rather than assumed; (3) GSVA per-sample Hallmark pathway scores (the 50 human Hallmark sets from the reference store) tested with limma using the same 2-group design, which directly answers 'a score for every hallmark signature in every sample' and 'which signatures differ'; (4) a combined report giving DE diagnostics, the Hallmark score matrix, the limma results per signature (BH-adjusted across the 50 signatures), and the reproducibility record. Reactome/WikiPathways/GO follow-up enrichment was not requested by the user (only Hallmark signatures) so it is left out to avoid unasked scope, per the plan-authoring rule against speculative additions; the DE step nonetheless anchors gene-level significance so the Hallmark scores are read alongside, not instead of, individual gene evidence.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
